issue: Does Brady v. Maryland require the prosecution to disclose exculpatory evidence to a defendant before the defendant pleads guilty?

sides.position: Brady's obligation to disclose exculpatory (not merely impeachment) evidence applies before a guilty plea, or at least the question is open and a defendant may challenge a plea on that basis.
cases: Sanchez v. United States, 50 F.3d 1448 (9th Cir. 1995)
United States v. Ohiri, 133 F. App'x 555 (10th Cir. 2005)

sides.position: No clear constitutional entitlement to exculpatory Brady material before a guilty plea; the Brady right does not extend to pre-plea disclosure in the plea-bargaining context.
cases: United States v. Mathur, 624 F.3d 498 (1st Cir. 2010)
United States v. Moussaoui, 591 F.3d 263 (4th Cir. 2010)
Alvarez v. City of Brownsville, 904 F.3d 382 (5th Cir. 2018) (en banc)
Mansfield v. Williamson County, 30 F.4th 276 (5th Cir. 2022)

this_court: Follows Alvarez (en banc) and does not recognize a pre-plea Brady right to exculpatory evidence; the majority states that only the Supreme Court can resolve the split.
quote: at the least definitively resolve the acknowledged circuit split.
cite: Mansfield v. Williamson Cty, 30 F.4th 276 (5th Cir. 2022)
